extracted.intended_audience: Registration Agencies (OA and SAAs), State CTE Agencies, potential program sponsors (LEAs, institutions of higher education, designated intermediaries), employers, and other registered apprenticeship stakeholders and commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory requirements and quality standards for establishing, approving, and administering Registered Career and Technical Education (CTE) apprenticeship programs, including coordination between Registration Agencies and State CTE Agencies, required program components, industry skills frameworks, instructional and on-the-job-hours minima, sponsor eligibility, and exemption process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-deregistration remediation evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agency may determine that a formerly deregistered sponsor's post-deregistration evidence (e.g., evidence of registering at least one apprentice and an adequate explanation for prior failure) demonstrates conformance with parts 29 and 30 and may treat the sponsor accordingly; what constitutes adequate evidence lies exclusively with the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: a sponsor deregistered for failing to register a single apprentice could later provide evidence of registering at least one apprentice plus an adequate explanation; determination of adequacy is sole province of the Registration Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption request process (§29.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for exemptions from any or all provisions in subpart A must be made in writing, transmitted to the Administrator, and contain a statement of the reasons supporting the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator will grant exemptions only for good cause; Department seeks comments on criteria for 'good cause.' The Department would not grant an exemption that would reduce or minimize protections afforded apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and authority for exemptions (§29.23) — limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator retains full and exclusive authority to evaluate and grant exemptions under proposed §29.23; SAAs are excluded from involvement in consideration or issuance of exemptions under that provision; the exemption provision would not apply to regulatory provisions in subparts B or C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision modeled on 29 CFR 30.19 but excludes SAA involvement; Department may consider comments on exemptions for subpart B but is not proposing exemption authority for subpart C because subpart C addresses data collection and SAA governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required coordination between Registration Agency and State CTE Agency (§29.24(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Registration Agency (OA or SAA) and the State CTE Agency must coordinate on administration of Registered CTE apprenticeship programs in each State to facilitate program approvals, program reviews, data collection, and compliance activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination aims to ensure welfare of CTE apprentices and administrative oversight; encourages joint industry engagement, services to employers, program promotion, and technical assistance. The Department requests comments on how to develop coordination and what elements to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written agreement requirement for statewide coordination (§29.24(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The State CTE Agency and Registration Agency must enter into a written agreement describing roles and responsibilities for statewide coordination and operation of Registered CTE apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may use MOUs, interagency agreements, or other written forms; Department expects flexibility but requires a formal understanding. Comments requested on what should be included and alignment with SAA State Apprenticeship Plan efforts and subpart C processes (e.g., data sharing, program review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core program registration requirements (§29.24 general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered CTE apprenticeship programs must meet core requirements: coordination with a Registration Agency and State CTE Agency; program standards and requirement that they be registered with a Registration Agency; alignment of competencies obtained through on-the-job training to approved industry skills frameworks; related instruction delivered through a CTE program; sponsor eligibility rules; partnership and coordination with employers and intermediaries; and written CTE apprenticeship agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list is intended as the foundational regulatory structure for CTE apprenticeship programs; the Department is interested in comments on these core requirements and possible additions or substantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and role of industry skills frameworks (§29.24(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry skills frameworks are a distinct required component of Registered CTE apprenticeship program standards and provide the basis for assessing competency and skill attainment in the on-the-job training component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should enable application of high-quality labor standards, be industry validated, rigorously developed, portable, and overseen/updated by the Administrator. They are similar to but distinct from National Occupational Standards (focus on industrywide competencies vs. occupational proficiency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry skills frameworks must include professional, workplace, and academic competencies (§29.24(b)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: An industry skills framework must include a structure for the development of professional behaviors (e.g., reliability, initiative, interpersonal skills, adaptability), workplace competencies (e.g., collaboration, oral and written communication, customer service), and academic competencies (e.g., reading, writing, problem-solving, critical thinking) required by an industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements form the foundational 'building blocks' for greater occupational proficiency and should be incorporated into program standards and related instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry skills frameworks validation and national applicability (§29.24(b)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry skills frameworks must be validated, widely recognized, and nationally applicable within the industry to which they apply, recognizing cross-cutting skills across industries and sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should align with CTE Career Clusters and State/local advisory council processes where possible; the Department anticipates broad industry stakeholder engagement in development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum on-the-job training hours for CTE apprentices (§29.24(b)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Skills and competencies specified within the on-the-job training outline must be obtained by a CTE apprentice through attainment of at least 900 hours of on-the-job training over the course of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 900 hours may be spread across multiple years. The Department considers a minimum OJT hour requirement important to ensure sufficient employment experience to obtain industrywide technical competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of industry skills framework with approved CTE program (§29.24(b)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: An industry skills framework must align with an approved CTE program so that the employment component provides appropriate practical on-the-job training supported by CTE apprenticeship-related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should align with the National Career Clusters® Framework and Advance CTE materials to enable cohesion and seamless transitions for CTE apprentices into employment, postsecondary education, or subpart A apprenticeship programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-validated methods for ongoing apprentice evaluations (§29.24(b)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry skills frameworks must detail industry-validated methods for ongoing evaluations to assess apprentices' attainment of competencies; regular evaluations are a required element of registered CTE apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and specifics of assessments/evaluations are left to program sponsors, consistent with the view that regular evaluations verify whether programs prepare apprentices for careers. High-quality CTE programs already perform such assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related instruction minimum hours and postsecondary credit (CTE-specific instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Registered CTE apprenticeship the Department proposes a minimum of 540 hours of required CTE apprenticeship-related instruction, which encompasses not less than 12 postsecondary credit hours as part of the program, paired with 900 hours of on-the-job training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a higher related instruction expectation than subpart A (which proposes 144 hours per 2,000 OJT) to ensure CTE apprentices meet academic requirements for graduation while limiting age-appropriate work hours for students. Instruction and OJT may occur while students are enrolled in high school or postsecondary education or span both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program outcomes and credentialing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Completing a Registered CTE apprenticeship program should provide CTE apprentices with industrywide skills and competencies, a recognized postsecondary credential(s), and at least 12 transferable postsecondary credit hours, enabling enrollment in postsecondary education, entry into employment, or entry/advanced standing in a subpart A registered apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are intended to strengthen pathways to employment and education; Department envisions nationally recognized certificates of completion and alignment that support transitions and stackable credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program sponsor eligibility and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible program sponsors for Registered CTE apprenticeship include LEAs, institutions of higher education, State CTE Agencies, or designated intermediaries, subject to program sponsor eligibility and program administration requirements described in proposed §29.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors must deliver related instruction through CTE programs, coordinate with Registration and State CTE Agencies, partner with employers and intermediaries, and implement program standards and agreements. The Department notes distinctions from subpart A sponsor eligibility and requests comments on sponsor roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for robust standards and apprentice protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered CTE apprenticeship programs are not exempt from establishment and implementation of robust standards to ensure consistently high-quality education and training and to ensure CTE apprentices are trained in a safe, accessible workplace environment protected from exploitation and abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department emphasizes safety, welfare, and protections for primarily school-aged and young adult apprentices; exemptions that would reduce protections will not be granted.
